summary: The native method mapping and public UTF-8 decoder are implemented cleanly, and the focused Go and compiled-ABAP tests pass. However, the Base64 step does not fully match Node for Unicode characters embedded in the encoded input, violating the requested handling of extraneous characters.

findings.claim: Reusing DecodeXBase64 loses Node compatibility for non-ASCII input. That helper scans UTF-8 bytes and discards every non-ASCII byte, whereas Node's Base64 decoder processes the low byte of each UTF-16 code unit. Consequently, DecodeBase64(nil, "YW😀JhcA==") returns "abap", but Node returns "a" because the high surrogate contributes a padding byte. Likewise, "YWŊhcA==" returns "ah\" instead of Node's "abap". The new text-decoding path needs Node-compatible input processing before Base64 decoding.
findings.repro:
cat > /tmp/review-b64-repro.go <<'EOF'
package main
import ("fmt"; "osg/gogen/abap")
func main() { fmt.Printf("%q\n", abap.DecodeBase64(nil, "YW😀JhcA==")) }
EOF
(cd tools/gogen/go && go run /tmp/review-b64-repro.go)
node -e 'console.log(JSON.stringify(Buffer.from("YW😀JhcA==", "base64").toString()))'
# Go: "abap"; Node: "a"
